name: faster-hex
verdict_reason: In const-hex's published run (Ryzen 9 7950X, 2024-10), faster-hex 0.10.0 encoded 5.9x-71x and decoded 6.2x-54x faster than hex 0.4 from 32 bytes to 1 MiB. faster-hex 1.0 (2026-09) is a rewrite with no published numbers in text yet.
tier_reason: Benchmark run by a third party (const-hex) with public code, the CPU and the rustc nightly stated.
claimed_speedup: encode 17.42 vs 102.11 ns (32 B), 42,883.20 vs 3,048,496.30 ns (1 MiB); decode 17.25 vs 107.13 ns (32 B), 118,576.16 vs 6,409,293.90 ns (1 MiB); 5.9x-71x encode, 6.2x-54x decode (ratios derived from page data)
workload: libtest #[bench] encode and decode (allocating String/Vec outputs) of 32 B, 256 B, 2 KiB, 16 KiB, 128 KiB and 1 MiB inputs.
platforms: x86 SSE4.1/AVX2 (AVX-512BW for validation and decoding), aarch64 NEON, portable fallback; no_std
one_liner: SIMD hex encoding and decoding, measured 6x-71x faster than the hex crate by a third party.
how_it_is_fast: Converts and validates a full SIMD register of bytes per step: SSE4.1 or AVX2 on x86 and NEON on aarch64, with AVX-512BW used for validation and decoding when the CPU has it. A portable fallback covers other targets.
use_it_when: Bulk hex encoding/decoding on x86_64 or aarch64
Hash-sized inputs (32 bytes) where it still beat hex by about 6x
skip_it_when: Versions before 0.10.1 with hex_decode_unchecked on x86: RUSTSEC-2026-0306
Toolchains older than 1.95, which faster-hex 1.0 requires
caveats: Numbers are for faster-hex 0.10.0; 1.0 was rewritten and is unmeasured in published text
const-hex's README says faster-hex is only optimized for x86, which is out of date: faster-hex's README now lists NEON
Nightly toolchain, libtest bench harness, one machine
tradeoffs: SIMD paths use unsafe; RUSTSEC-2026-0306 (2026-09-20) found the AVX2 path of the safe hex_decode_unchecked reading past its input in 0.3.0-0.10.0

evidence.quote: The following benchmarks were ran on an AMD Ryzen 9 7950X, compiled with `1.83.0-nightly (9ff5fc4ff 2024-10-03)` on `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`.
Uses SSE4.1 or AVX2 on x86 and NEON on AArch64 when available, with AVX-512BW acceleration for validation and decoding.
